First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +4 & =0 \\ {(\lambda -2)}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =2$ is a repeated root, and therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{2x}+Bx{e}^{2x}.
$$

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $13\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x,
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x} & =-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡3x+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡3x \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =-9\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x-9\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x\end{aligned}
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
(-9\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x-9\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x)-4(-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡3x+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡3x)+4(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3x)=13\operatorname{sin}⁡3x
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(-5\alpha -12\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡3x+(12\alpha -5\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡3x=13\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-5\alpha -12\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3x) \\ 12\alpha -5\beta =13\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =\frac{12}{13}$ and $\beta =-\frac{5}{13}.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\frac{12}{13}\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{2x}+Bx{e}^{2x}+\frac{12}{13}\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{sin}⁡3x.
$$
